items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: The interviewer mentions Eddie Miller in the context of Louis Prima's band ('people like Eddie Miller and George Brunis... with him'). The interviewee (Johnny Wiggs) responds with 'Oh, yeah, yeah.' There is no statement from Johnny Wiggs indicating he personally knew, played with, or collaborated wi

ctx.x: Johnny said that nobody hurt him. I can't think of his name right now. But he played against Louis Armstrong on a boat, and Louis Armstrong put his horn down, said that he could pass Emmett Hardy that I'm talking about.
Yeah, the man who never recorded, Eddie.

He never did record, no, because he didn't have the chance. But there were so many great trumpet players, like Red Borman, that was another great trumpet man. And it takes quite a few. In fact, I mean, we have still some fine jazz men, but they just don't get together. And when they don't get together, what they do, they organize the band, and they'll organize to their satisfaction. They get a drum player that don't know the beats, and then they call themselves. items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I was going to use Snoozer Quinn on guitar and Siegfried Christensen on piano and Eddie Miller on clarinet and I was going to play cornet

ctx.x: I don't know what Celestine was doing. It was Schatz for a while. It was Schatz Madison.

I don't know, but one of them was a mean man and the other one was, one trumpet player was a mean guy and the other one was a very nice fellow. Well, I set them to rehearsing across, Wailines had a sort of a warehouse across the street and without getting any permission because I knew I couldn't get permission for this, I just took it upon myself to take them over there.
